title: Object: Mark init and cleanup code as cold

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

Our class initialization and binding code (`_bind_methods` in all `GDCLASS`es) and registration (`register_*_types`, `initialize_*_module`) code makes up a significant portion of our binary size due to `-O3` optimization causing inlining of String/StringName constructor/destructor, CowData reference counting, Variant handling, maybe some other things.

This is something @Ivorforce has started handling by trying to limit the code inlined for some of those heavily used types, e.g. #123984.

But I found that GCC and Clang have a [`cold`](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Common-Attributes.html#index-cold) attribute that we could try to use to mark the init and cleanup code as cold, meaning that it's unlikely to be called (never in a hot path), and thus the compiler can optimize it for size (like it would with `-Os`/`-Oz`, limiting inlining).

So this PR adds a `_COLD_` macro which sets `__attribute__((cold))` for GCC and Clang-based compilers. It's applied to `GDCLASS` initialization, which, for GCC, propagates to all `_bind_methods` so we don't need to flag each `_bind_methods` declaration as `_COLD_` explicitly (which would impact hundreds of files). Sadly, Clang doesn't seem to propagate `cold` the same way, so it doesn't benefit it.

With GCC, this PR saves **2.40 MiB** on a Linux `template_release` (**-3.2%**) and **3.60 MiB** on a Linux `editor` (**-2.8%**).
It only saves 0.88 MiB (-1.1%) on Windows mingw-gcc, but that may be partially caused by a workaround we have now which seems to limit LTO efficiency, which I'll look into.
With Clang on Linux, it only saves ~70 KiB. With Emscripten, it very slightly increases the wasm size (20 KiB, +0.06%).

Some throwaway behavior and performance benchmarks (AI made) found no difference in the API generation, no performance impact, and no build time change.

Untested on MSVC, where `_COLD_` would be a no-op but the other `GDCLASS` changes would need to be validated too.

Keeping as draft for now because overall, while the gains seem very interesting for GCC, there are still a lot of unknowns, and I can't claim to fully understand the implications of `cold` on our code for GCC and all Clang-based compilers.

Some of those gains may also be achievable through other means which will benefit all compilers (such as carefully changing core code to limit unwanted inlining).

Overall, profile guided optimization may be a much better approach of achieving similar/better gains by rooting the compiler choices into real usage data. But I have no idea on how to even start with that :D
